text.p: Australia's Liberal-National government will hand down its 1997/98 budget on May 13, according to the official parliamentary programme.
Prime Minister John Howard, elected in March, had indicated he would revive the practice of a May announcement for the budget for the July-June fiscal year.
The 1996/97 budget, delayed by national elections, was released on August 20.
After ending 13 years of Labor rule, Howard's conservative government announced it would slash spending to wipe out the deficit over three years.
The 1996/97 budget cut spending by almost A$4 billion and halved the underlying deficit to A$5.3 billion from A$10.6 billion in 1994/95.
The underlying deficit excludes windfall items such as asset sales and debt repayments by state governments.
